disclaimer: Source of the raw materials that the regional exchange sells in the cities (D-120). A new world has no natural ore (the scarcity package); these finite, shared, slowly refilling shelves, salvage and one regenerating resource site are where iron, coal, copper, redstone, lapis, gold and diamonds come from. Run scripts/generate_survival_supply.py to regenerate rpg-core/src/main/resources/data/underground_city/regional_stock/materials. Prices are credits per item; a full shelf is worth at most 1200 credits.

lines.why: Ironhaven's foundries sell what they can spare from their own furnaces: the cheapest iron in the region, a small shelf that refills in a steady trickle.
Furnace coal from the foundries' own stocks, a few credits a lump.
Cable and fitting copper from Ironhaven's rolling mills; the second backpack tier is eight ingots round a basic pack.
Valewood's charcoal burners supply the region's kilns and smithies with a fuel that needs no mine.
Valewood buys its iron in from Ironhaven and sells it on at a premium, a few ingots at a time, so that a Valewood household need not travel for a hinge or a hoe.
Blackwater's electronics wholesalers import redstone dust by the sack and sell it by the handful.
Imported through the harbour from Ironhaven, so dearer than at the source.
Dye and optics stock that the harbour's importers hold for the glassworks.
The harbour's bullion dealers sell a few bars at a time; gold is a fitting for the finest work, not a stockpile.
One gem every two active hours from the harbour's jewellers: the fifth backpack tier is a long-term purchase, not an afternoon's.
